findings.evidence: develop/SKILL.md already uses 'Phase D' sub-headings D.1 / D.2 / D.3 for *lane execution modes*: 'D.1 Green-lane batched execution' (line 403), 'D.2 Yellow-lane HITL pairing' (line 424), 'D.3 Red-lane human-led with bounded AI assistance' (line 430). The PRD's R1 + AC-1 prescribe new sub-headings 'D.1 Red', 'D.2 Green', 'D.3 Refactor' inside the same Phase D — and R7 + AC-10 *also* require the existing Red lane (PROTECTED_PATHS_REQUIRE_RED_LANE) to remain intact and unchanged in routing. The PRD therefore mandates two parallel D.1/D.2/D.3 axes (Red/Green/Refactor cycle vs Green/Yellow/Red lane) under the same headings. AC-1's grep `^### D\.[123]` cannot disambiguate which axis a given heading represents. The verbatim string 'Red' under '### D.1 Red' will collide with the 'Red lane' which AC-10 separately protects.
findings.claim: Architectural gotcha: the PRD silently overloads the existing D.1/D.2/D.3 numbering. develop/SKILL.md cannot host both 'D.1 Red (TDD cycle)' AND 'D.1 Green-lane batched execution' under one Phase D — the structural collision is unaddressed in the PRD. Downstream cost: AC-1's verification grep is ambiguous; AC-10's 'Red-lane unchanged' check competes with AC-1's '### D.1 Red'; the post-change SKILL.md cannot satisfy both literally.
findings.proposed_change: Add an explicit decision in the PRD on how the cycle sub-phases coexist with the lane sub-phases. Two viable shapes: (a) rename the cycle sub-phases to a non-colliding scheme — e.g. D.1 plan-execution unfolds *as* Red→Green→Refactor inside whatever lane (Green/Yellow/Red) the task landed on, and the markers carry the cycle identity rather than headings; (b) renumber the existing lane sections to D.4/D.5/D.6 (or move them under a Phase D.0 'lane dispatch') and keep D.1/D.2/D.3 for the cycle. Pick one in the PRD before tasks are written; AC-1's grep needs to resolve to exactly one set of headings.

findings.evidence: 029-single-context-task-prd.md R6 reads: 'Phases D/E/F of `specflow:develop` carry a *single one-line reminder* citing the doctrine doc as the canonical "no mid-task compaction" reference. The compaction-is-a-defect-signal stance is *not* duplicated in the skill body' — citing `feedback_skill_size_ceiling` (chain-don't-absorb). 017's R1 + R2 + R3 + R5 + R6 expand Phase D's body substantively (three new sub-phases, each with bounding clauses, conditional verify steps for `tddRequired`, no-new-files hard-block detection per R11, manifest-marker schema in R9). The current develop/SKILL.md is already 710 lines (verified via Read). 017's expansions add at minimum: D.1 Red prose + invocation contract, D.2 Green verify-conditional, D.3 Refactor bounds + hard-block path, plus a CORE_PRINCIPLES TDD section and a config schema entry. None of the requirements cite the single-context doctrine doc as the home for the cycle contract.
findings.claim: Cross-artefact drift / blast-radius underestimate: 029 just shipped (commit b2e4ee9) with the explicit chain-don't-absorb stance for develop's Phase D. 017 absorbs the cycle into develop/SKILL.md instead of chaining via a doctrine doc analogous to `templates/admin/single-context-task.md`. The PRD should either (a) follow 029's pattern and create a TDD doctrine doc that develop's Phase D cites, or (b) explicitly call out the deviation and justify it. Right now it does neither — the absorption is silent.
findings.proposed_change: Add a requirement (e.g. R0 or amended R1) creating `plugins/specflow/templates/admin/tdd-discipline.md` as the doctrine home for the Red→Green→Refactor contract, the bounds, the marker schema, and the `tddRequired` semantics. develop/SKILL.md Phase D adds three sub-phase headings + one-line invocation contracts + a single citation back to the doctrine doc — mirroring 029's R6. This pre-empts the skill-size-ceiling violation the current shape will hit.

findings.evidence: Interview Round 4 explicitly says the markers are 'internal to the task's single context window — they help the agent (and the retro reader) see the cycle structure' and Gate 5's reviewers 'see the assembled change set' (not the manifest). PRD R9's schema-dependency clause + AC-7c specify a fallback: 'Until 019-per-task-manifest lands, 017 writes the three lines into a stub `## Per-task manifest stub` section appended at the bottom of `{NNN-slug}-tasks.md` per task; 019 absorbs the section when it lands.' But `{NNN-slug}-tasks.md` is read by every downstream skill: develop's Phase A.1 reads tasks.md (SKILL.md:80), test's Phase A.1 reads tasks.md (test/SKILL.md:64), develop's resume logic at Phase A reads tasks.md, the cross-task reviewer (022) reads tasks.md. The stub is not internal — it's broadcast.
findings.claim: Cross-artefact drift between interview and PRD: interview frames markers as 'internal to the single context window' but PRD R9's stub fallback writes them into the canonical tasks artefact every downstream skill reads. The 'internal' framing dies the moment the fallback fires. Worse, AC-10's R9 schema is owned by 017 but read 'unchanged' by 019 — coupling that doesn't exist today. If 019 doesn't ship before another consumer (test? scope-change? complete?) starts reading the stub, the schema's read surface grows beyond 017's control without an explicit consumer contract.
findings.proposed_change: Either (a) honour the 'internal' framing by writing markers to a scratch file the agent owns within the single context window — e.g. `admin/scratch/{NNN-slug}-develop/manifest-stub-{task-id}.md` — and let 019 promote from scratch when it lands, OR (b) drop the 'internal' framing in the interview and treat the manifest as a published artefact from day one (which means R9 needs a consumer-contract clause naming who reads the stub between now and 019). The PRD currently picks neither — interview says internal, R9 picks a tasks.md location that is the most-broadcast artefact in the system.

findings.evidence: PRD touches: (1) develop/SKILL.md Phase D restructure + per-task verify-conditional + Refactor hard-block + manifest-marker emission [R1, R2, R3, R5, R6, R9, R11], (2) test/SKILL.md `--plan-only` flag extension with `--task` co-flag [R8, AC-6], (3) CORE_PRINCIPLES.md new TDD section [R12, AC-9], (4) admin/config.json schema new `develop.tddRequired` field [R6, AC-5], (5) `{NNN-slug}-tasks.md` stub-section appendix [R9 schema-dependency, AC-7c], (6) `{NNN-slug}-test.md` carries the Red artefact [R8]. Five files + two artefact shapes. CORE_PRINCIPLES.md is loaded into *every* specflow skill's system prompt (CORE_PRINCIPLES.md line 1 + line 70 'Both ship to every skill's system prompt'); R12 therefore expands every skill's system prompt size — a blast radius the PRD does not enumerate.
findings.claim: Blast-radius underestimate / lane-surface mismatch: a Yellow-lane PRD (paired-HITL execution, this is the dogfood project) touching five files + two artefact shapes including a system-prompt-loaded principles file is plausibly Red-lane territory by blast radius alone. CORE_PRINCIPLES.md changes propagate to every skill's prompt cache invalidation, every gate reviewer's framing, every future PRD's R-trace surface — that's high blast radius (>3 files, cross-module per the lane-triage axes in develop/SKILL.md:134). The PRD's 'Surgical' framing in goals/non-goals does not acknowledge this.
findings.proposed_change: Add a 'Blast radius' section to the PRD (or amend Vision) enumerating the five files + the cache-invalidation cost on CORE_PRINCIPLES.md + the schema-coupling cost on tasks.md/manifest. State the lane the PRD expects this work to run on (Yellow vs Red). If it stays Yellow, justify the per-axis call. If R12 (CORE_PRINCIPLES.md change) is the surface that pushes it to Red, consider deferring R12 (per simplicity-r1-f2's proposal) and shipping the Phase D restructure in Yellow alone.

findings.evidence: PRD R3(b) + R11 + AC-4 + AC-11 specify Refactor's 'no new files' bound. Existing develop/SKILL.md already carries scope-protection mechanisms: (i) B.1.2/B.1.3 mechanical pre-Gate-4 lane recheck downgrades blast radius if `modules_plan_vs_scope.new_modules` is non-empty (line 246), (ii) Phase B.1.3 force-upgrades to Red on confidential-path-detected-mid-execution (line 247-248), (iii) Phase D.1 'Machine-check failure mid-task' force-upgrades Green→Yellow (line 422), (iv) failure mode 'Confidential-path detected mid-execution' (line 648) force-upgrades to Red. The non-negotiable rule registry already contains PROTECTED_PATHS_REQUIRE_RED_LANE. None of these existing mechanisms detect 'agent created a new file during the Refactor sub-phase that wasn't in the Green-end file set' — that is a *new* detection axis (Green-end-file-set vs Refactor-end-file-set diff, scoped to the single context window).
findings.claim: Architectural gotcha: R11's 'hard-block on new files in Refactor' is novel detection logic with no existing host. The proposed change in simplicity-r1-f5 ('the existing scope-change route already covers it') is wrong — the existing routes detect *plan-vs-actual* drift (B.1.3) or *machine-check* failure (D.1) or *confidentiality* path matches (B.1.3 / failure modes). None of them detect 'file count grew between Green and Refactor sub-phases of the same task within the same single context window.' R11 either needs new tracking inside D.3 (snapshot file set at Green end, diff at Refactor end) or it ships as documented-prose-only without enforcement.
findings.proposed_change: Add a concrete enforcement clause to R11: name the snapshot mechanism (e.g. 'agent emits `green-end-files.json` to scratch at Green-end; Refactor-end compares against it before commit') OR demote R11 to documented-prose with a manifest-marker outcome value `refactor: failed (new-file-attempted)` so retros can catch the violation post-hoc. The current R11 + AC-11 wording assumes detection exists; it doesn't.
